subject: AtlasPay reserved capacity lurch — urgent remediation & exec attention
messages:
From: AtlasPay Ops <ops@atlaspay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-21T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike on reserved pool (US)

Kim,

We started seeing sustained latency increases around 08:50 PDT and a rise in 5xx errors for our /generate endpoint. Throughput for our reserved capacity appears to have dropped ~28% compared to the same window yesterday — requests are queueing and hitting your backend fallback more frequently. We're in peak transaction window and this is causing user-visible failures.

Key observations: 
- Latency p95 jumped from ~230ms to ~1200ms between 08:50–09:10
- 5xx rate rose to 3.6% (baseline ~0.2%)
- Reserved capacity utilization charts show token throughput dip despite steady incoming QPS (attached throughput_metrics_20280621.csv)

We already toggled to the hosted fallback for a subset of traffic but the application cannot sustain degraded models long-term. This is impacting checkout flows (~4% drop in conversions).

We need an immediate short-term mitigation (burst or temporary reallocation) and a committed timeline for a fix. Please escalate if needed — our procurement and SLA teams are on standby.

Regards,
Rahul Malhotra
Sr. Ops Engineer, AtlasPay
ops@atlaspay.com

Attachment: throughput_metrics_20280621.csv
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: AtlasPay Ops <ops@atlaspay.com>, J. Patel <sla@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-21T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike on reserved pool (US)

Rahul — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We're looking at the metrics now. I confirmed receipt of your CSV and we've pulled the subset of request traces (snippet attached).

Immediate actions (30–90m):
- Temporary routing: we've opened a targeted fallback route for non-critical checkout validation flows to the hosted layer to relieve token contention (already in progress).
- Emergency slot swap: requesting authorization to borrow 20% extra reserved throughput from our burst pool for AtlasPay for the next 4 hours — this requires exec sign-off (see Marcus/Irene).
- Debug: infra team is tracing the KV cache hit-rate and kernel scheduling for the hot model; preliminary signal shows increased KV misses on a handful of shards (redwood-inference-log-snippet.txt attached).

I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until the window stabilizes. If you can share any client-side traffic anomalies or correlation ids, please send them. Apologies for the disruption — we understand the conversion impact.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-inference-log-snippet.txt
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike on reserved pool (AtlasPay) — urgent exec ask

Marcus / Irene — forwarding the AtlasPay incident. TL;DR: reserved token throughput for their US reserved pool dropped ~28% during their morning peak (08:50–09:10 PDT), causing higher queueing/5xx and materially impacting revenue. They've already routed some traffic to hosted fallback which degrades latency/cost for them.

Why I'm escalating:
- This is a top-20 customer by ARR with a contract that includes a 99.9% token throughput SLA for reserved capacity during business hours (deal: DEAL-78912).
- Short-term borrow (20% reserved throughput, 4 hours) will likely avert customer-visible outages, but procurement needs confirmation and billing/credit sign-off.
- Ops signals indicate a shard-level KV-cache miss cascade; quick mitigation could be an intra-cluster slot realignment or a temporary recompile to a fallback kernel — both need infra coordination.

Asks: 
1) Marcus — can you approve an emergency reserve reallocation + one-time credit (we should offer a partial service credit and waive the burst fee for the period)?
2) Irene — please convene infra/rt-ng to run the KV-cache probe and decide whether a hot-shard migration or runtime patch is needed.
3) If either of you want me to elevate to the CTO / CEO, say so and I'll pull them in.

I'm standing by on the 30-minute updates to AtlasPay. Will include timelines and suggested customer communication once we align.

—Kim
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: AtlasPay Ops <ops@atlaspay.com>, J. Patel <sla@atlaspay.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-23T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPay reserved capacity lurch — remediation summary and next steps

Rahul / J. Patel — thank you for your patience while we investigated. Summary of actions taken and status: 

What we did (timeline):
- 2028-06-21 09:10 PDT: Emergency slot swap — we reallocated +22% reserved throughput for AtlasPay from our burst pool; this restored p95 latency to ~260ms for critical flows within 12 minutes.
- 2028-06-21 11:00 PDT: Infra ran KV-cache consistency probes and remapped 3 hot shards away from a congested host; kernel fallback disabled after verification.
- 2028-06-22 02:00 PDT: Nightly reconcile uncovered a model-side quantization edge-case that increased memory pressure under a specific token distribution; a targeted runtime patch was rolled to the affected nodes (no restart required).

Customer-facing commitments: 
- Short-term: the emergency throughput reallocation will be billed at zero burst fee and we'll issue a 10% service credit for the affected 4-hour window (see attached credit_note_draft link).
- Medium-term: engineering will prioritize an infra hardening ticket (INF-2142) to add proactive shard-evacuation when KV-cache miss-rate > 12% for sustained 3m windows, targeted delivery in the July release.
- Long-term: we'll schedule a joint post-mortem and runbook review with AtlasPay the week of 2028-07-09.

What to watch for: sustained KV-miss hotspots, token distribution skew during peak windows, and any cross-tenant noisy neighbor signals. Marcus (cc'd) will track the INF-2142 ticket and provide weekly updates.

Rahul — can we schedule a 30-minute remediation readout tomorrow to close the loop and confirm the credit/contract notes? I attached the metrics and logs we referenced.

—Marcus Lin
VP, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
